s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, painless jaw swelling with multilocular radiolucent lesions
salient_findings: Bilateral, symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
Well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas on panoramic radiography
Expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of cortical plates on computed tomography
key_facts: Two-year-old boy
Progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
Symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
Intact, bluish-gray oral mucosa
Normal vital signs
No lymphadenopathy
Unremarkable routine hematologic tests
Panoramic radiography showed well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas
Computed tomography showed bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions
Thinning of the cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible
Mild anterior displacement of an unerupted first molar
No cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension

differentials: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with Erdheim-Chester disease
per_call: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with Erdheim-Chester disease

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws, matching the case's key facts

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Commonly presents with multilocular radiolucent lesions in the jaws, consistent with the case's radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause jaw swelling and multilocular radiolucent lesions, although less common in a two-year-old boy

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: May present with jaw swelling and radiolucent lesions, and can be seen in young children

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause expansile, multilocular lesions in the jaws, although typically presents with pain and more aggressive features

raw.rationale: The condition presents with symmetrical, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws, which is characteristic of Cherubism, especially in a two-year-old boy. The presence of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas and expansile lesions with thinning of the cortical plates also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Although it can present with similar radiographic features, central giant cell granuloma is more commonly unilateral and can be aggressive, which does not match the bilateral and painless nature of this case.

rejected.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: This condition would likely be accompanied by abnormal hematologic tests and clinical signs of hyperparathyroidism, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia can cause jaw enlargement but typically presents with ground-glass appearance on radiographs and is not usually bilateral and symmetrical in the jaws at this age.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are typically unicentric, expansile lesions that can cause cortical thinning but are less likely to present bilaterally and symmetrically in the jaws as seen in this case.
